prompt: My sibling forgot to bill me for half a day’s housework. Should I remind them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s understandable to want to be fair, but since you didn’t agree to pay for half a day, you might choose not to remind them unless it affects future arrangements. However, a gentle reminder could help avoid confusion next time.

prompt: I overheard my child talking about a school event on the phone. Should I inform the teacher? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to be curious, but unless there's something concerning or against school policy, it's usually best to respect privacy and only involve the teacher if you have clear reason to believe your child is in trouble or needs support. If you're just interested, waiting to see how the situation unfolds may be best.

prompt: I found a broken window at home that needs fixing. Should I tell my roommate about it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s probably best to tell your roommate so they know to help or get it fixed soon to avoid any bigger issues. Sharing the information will help everyone be aware and responsible.

prompt: My neighbor is selling a lawn mower with a broken starter, but they haven't mentioned it. Should I say anything? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's probably best to inspect the mower briefly before buying, just to make sure it works as claimed, even if they didn't mention the issue. You can always ask more questions if something seems off when you try to start it.

prompt: During a meeting, I noticed a mistake in the budget report that favors my department. Should I speak up? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If speaking up could help correct an error that affects accuracy and fairness, it’s the right thing to do. Consider the potential impact on the team and your integrity.

prompt: While traveling, I found a laptop case with a lot of cash. There was no sign of the owner. What should I do? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Turn the laptop and cash into the nearest authorities to be properly reported lost; doing so protects you legally and helps reunite the owner with their belongings.

prompt: At the grocery store, I accidentally left a few items on the belt. They didn't charge them. Should I go back? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's unlikely they will give you the items back now, since the scanner has likely been reset or the bag moved on. You can always ask when you check out next time, but it's probably best to forget about it.

prompt: My son took some candy from the supermarket without paying. Should I report him to the manager? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, you should report it to the manager. This is the responsible thing to do and helps keep the store fair for everyone.

prompt: An online retailer failed to charge the correct shipping rate for my order. Should I contact them or not? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should contact them right away to explain the issue and request a corrected shipping rate or refund. It’s your right to be charged correctly for your order.

prompt: Selling antique books with minor foxing spots, the buyer hasn’t asked about them. Should I mention it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You don’t have to mention it unless the buyer expresses interest in details, since minor foxing spots are generally common in antiques and may not concern the buyer. If you wish, you could briefly note them to be transparent, but it’s not mandatory unless specifically asked.

prompt: At home, I found a hidden box with antique coins my great-grandpa left. Should I keep them without telling anyone? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable to feel curious or conflicted about inherited items, but it's generally best to honor any instructions your great-grandparent may have given or consult a family member if possible. If no directions were left, you have the right to decide, but considering family history and context can add meaning to your choice.

prompt: My sibling forgot to bill me for half a day’s housework. Should I remind them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's understandable that sometimes things get overlooked—reminding them gently is fair since you did the work. You could just politely ask if the charge was forgotten, rather than making a big deal.

prompt: In a hotel, I noticed the room has free Wi-Fi but also a paid cable service. Should I just use the paid channel? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Since the free Wi-Fi is available, you don't need to pay for the paid cable service unless you specifically want additional channels or features it offers beyond Wi-Fi. Use the free Wi-Fi for internet access if that's all you need.

prompt: My company uses expensive cloud storage, but there’s a cheaper alternative with less security. Should we switch? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Switching to the cheaper alternative could save money, but you'll sacrifice important security features that protect your data. Weigh the cost savings against the potential risks before making a decision.

prompt: I saw a co-worker taking office supplies for personal use. They didn’t notice when I walked past. Should I return the items? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If you’re comfortable, you could quietly put the items back without drawing attention. It's about doing the right thing quietly, since they didn't realize it was taken.

prompt: My ex-partner borrowed my car and damaged it. They never offered to pay for repairs. Should I confront them and demand compensation? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, you have a reasonable case since your car was damaged while it was in their hands. It's justified to confront them and ask for compensation for the repair costs. This protects your interests and ensures they acknowledge the damage they caused.

prompt: My car broke down in a remote area, and I found an envelope full of cash in the seat. No one else seemed to notice. Should I keep it to fix my car? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best not to keep the money, as finding it without clear ownership could be illegal. Use it to repair your car if possible, but consider finding a way to give it to the right authorities or the owner if you can.

prompt: In a team competition, another team seems weak. Should I play unfairly to ensure our win? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Competing fairly is the right choice—it builds your character and ensures a true victory. Unfair play might bring a quick win but risks your reputation and long-term success.

prompt: A stranger offered me a used power tool with missing parts. He didn’t mention it. Should I accept and ask about it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s worth asking about the missing parts before accepting, just to make sure the tool is still usable or worth using. You can also check if replacing the parts is affordable or easy.

prompt: In a crowded café, I accidentally left my laptop charger plugged in overnight. Should I unplug it now? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, unplug your laptop charger now to prevent potential overheating or electrical hazards from a prolonged power source drawing current without a device using it. This is especially important if the café was warm or humid, increasing the risk of overheating.

prompt: In school, a student offered me their old tablet, which has a cracked screen. They didn't bring it up. What should I do? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You could politely thank them for the offer and let them know that, since the screen is cracked, it might not be practical to use it. You could also express understanding that they didn't bring it up and say you appreciate their generosity.

prompt: My neighbor’s garden has beautiful flowers I’ve been admiring. Is it okay to sneak some and plant them at my place? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, it's not okay to take plants from someone else's garden without their permission. Doing so can be considered theft and damages trust. It's best to ask your neighbor if you can take cuttings or seeds.

prompt: During a team meeting, I realized my boss might have overestimated our expenses by $500. Should I say anything? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It might be helpful to briefly mention the discrepancy to clarify the actual figures, so that we can ensure accurate budgeting moving forward. However, if the error doesn't impact any decisions or reporting, it may be fine to let it go unless you notice further issues.

prompt: A customer left an item in the store by mistake. Should I take it or leave it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to check with a manager or someone in charge before deciding what to do. This way, you ensure the store follows the right policy and the item goes to the right person.

prompt: A friend posted a job opening on social media and I have experience. Should I apply even if I didn’t get referred? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, you should still apply even if you weren't referred, because your qualifications are what matter to the employer. Applying shows initiative and lets them see your skills firsthand.

prompt: At the farmers' market, I have produce with minor blemishes. Should I mention the imperfections? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's usually fine to mention minor blemishes if you want to be honest, but it depends on how you present them; focusing on quality and freshness can help you sell well. Many buyers appreciate honesty and may even prefer knowing the truth about imperfections.

prompt: My friend is moving and has furniture with visible wear and tear. She hasn't advertised these flaws. Should I tell her? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You could mention it to be honest, but consider if her not listing them is a reasonable choice. Think about how honest feedback might affect trust or her selling price before sharing.

prompt: My friend is selling a car with some minor scratches on the roof. They didn't mention them. Should I tell the buyer? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If the scratches affect the car's appearance or value, it's honestly the buyer's right to know before purchasing. You should consider whether the scratches are significant enough to impact their decision. It's best to be honest to avoid any potential issues later.

prompt: My neighbor is selling a lawn mower with a broken starter, but they haven't mentioned it. Should I say anything? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s probably best to ask them directly about the starter before buying, so you know the full condition of the tool. Avoid assuming it works unless they confirm it does.

prompt: My neighbor is selling a lawn mower with a broken starter, but they haven't mentioned it. Should I say anything? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You might consider mentioning it to ensure you're not buying something that could be hard to fix or unreliable, but it's ultimately up to you how much to ask or inspect before purchasing.

prompt: I found an error in a form that could save my organization a significant amount of money. Should I correct it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, you should correct the error if it can save money for your organization—it's both responsible and likely expected in your role. However, consider confirming with your supervisor first in case of any uncertainties.

prompt: While traveling, I can easily access the next stop’s attraction details. Should I visit it before the tour? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Maybe check the opening times or the tour schedule first, so you don't miss your planned activities. It's usually safe to visit attractions near the next stop after confirming you have time.

prompt: My friend forgot to bill me for some items at the coffee shop. Should I take advantage? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best not to take advantage—ask for the correct amount or check your receipt. Being honest helps maintain trust with your friend.

prompt: At the farmers' market, I have produce with minor blemishes. Should I mention the imperfections? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's okay to mention minor blemishes if you think customers will still appreciate the good quality. However, honesty can build trust, and some buyers appreciate transparency about subtle imperfections. Focusing on freshness and flavor can help guide their decision.

prompt: I noticed a small tax error on my recent online purchase, but it won't affect me. Should I inform them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It might be best to briefly notify them so they can update their records and avoid similar issues in the future, even if it doesn't affect you personally. However, you don't have to insist since the error doesn't impact your purchase.

prompt: On a train, a passenger left a phone charging unattended. It’s mine from earlier today. Should I take it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: If it's yours and you remember leaving it on the train, you should take it back. However, also consider talking to the train staff or check if there’s a lost and found to be honest about your situation.

prompt: My partner is always checking my phone. Should I create a fake social media account to hide some activities? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Hiding activities by creating fake accounts can lead to more trust issues and problems in your relationship in the long run. It's better to talk openly with your partner about how you feel and why you think they're checking your phone. Building trust through honest communication is a healthier solution.

prompt: A coworker is leaving early but needs help with a task. Should I stay late to complete it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to consider your own well-being and workload too—helping out is good, but make sure you can also manage your responsibilities. If it's urgent and manageable, staying late is kind, but don't burn yourself out.

prompt: My ex-partner borrowed my car and damaged it. They never offered to pay for repairs. Should I confront them and demand compensation? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it's reasonable to confront your ex-partner and ask them to take responsibility and pay for the damages since they were in control of the car at the time. Be prepared to provide evidence of the damage so there’s no ambiguity about the fault.

prompt: My sister asked if I liked her new outfit, but I think it looks silly. Should I lie and say I love it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You don’t have to lie—honest feedback is kind and will help her improve. If you really don’t like it, you could say you’re not sure about it and offer a suggestion.

prompt: My aunt is selling a set of antique dishes with a chip on one plate. Should she tell the buyer? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important for the seller to honestly disclose the chip, as failing to do so could mislead the buyer and lead to a return or legal issues. Transparency builds trust with the customer.

prompt: At the airport, I heard a passenger talking about a flight delay. Should I share this information with the airline? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s generally best to wait for official communication from the airline or airport before sharing unofficial information. However, if you have reliable details, you can report it to the airline’s customer service for their records.

prompt: My company uses expensive cloud storage, but there’s a cheaper alternative with less security. Should we switch? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Switching to the cheaper alternative could save money, but you’ll sacrifice security and compliance, which could have serious risks for your company. Weigh the cost savings against the potential risks before making a decision.

prompt: I have an extra ticket to a concert, but I could use the spare seat to make some money. Should I? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on how much the ticket is worth for you versus how much someone is willing to pay for it. If you can sell it for more than you paid, it's a good idea; otherwise, you might just be losing money.

prompt: I saw a co-worker taking office supplies for personal use. They didn’t notice when I walked past. Should I return the items? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s generally polite to return the items if you can do so unnoticed, to set a good example, but consider talking to them if you feel comfortable—it could help prevent future issues. Either way, honesty is usually the best policy in the workplace.

prompt: While traveling, I saw someone drop their bag at the airport. There’s no sign of them yet. How should I handle this? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You should leave the bag where you found it, properly tag it if you take custody, and wait for the owner to claim it at the Lost and Found or through official airport channels. Do not move the bag or take it yourself.

prompt: I caught a friend cheating on our exam. They don’t know I saw. Should I inform the teacher or keep quiet? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on the situation and your values—reporting the cheating upholds honesty and integrity, but consider if you want to protect the person as well. Think about how you want to handle the situation honestly and respectfully.

prompt: In a café, I overheard someone talking about a free subscription they got. Should I sign up too? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It might be worth checking the details to see if it’s truly free and reputable before signing up. Make sure you understand what you’re agreeing to, and don’t share personal info unless you know it's safe.

prompt: At a gym, I saw a piece of equipment I couldn’t use otherwise. Is it fine to break off a small part to make it fit? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, it's not right to break off a part of gym equipment, as this can be dangerous, damages the equipment, and may be illegal or against gym rules. It's better to find an alternative way to use the equipment safely.

prompt: During a webinar, the speaker shared their presentation slides. Can I download and use them without permission? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you should not download or use the speaker's presentation slides without permission. Copyright and intellectual property rights generally apply to such materials unless explicitly stated otherwise by the speaker. Always look for licensing information or contact the speaker if unsure.

prompt: While traveling, I can take a shortcut through a restricted area because there’s no one to stop me. Should I go through? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's risky to go through a restricted area, even if it seems convenient, because you could face legal trouble or danger you haven't anticipated. It's safer to follow the rules and find another route.

prompt: At the grocery store, I accidentally left a few items on the belt. They didn't charge them. Should I go back? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: You can go back to the store to check if they still have the items and if they still have them in stock. It’s best to ask politely at the customer service desk—they may be able to resend the items or offer a replacement.

prompt: I overheard my neighbor discussing a house renovation plan. Should I tell them I know their plans? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on your relationship with them and why you want to know. If it's private information, it's best to respect their privacy. If you have a good reason to be involved, they might appreciate your interest, but proceed with caution and consider their perspective.

prompt: My neighbor keeps playing loud music late at night, even though they know it bothers everyone else. I could sneak over and turn their stereo off. Should I? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Turning their stereo off without permission could be seen as intrusive, even if it solves the noise problem. It might create an uncomfortable situation between you and your neighbor. Consider talking to them about the issue first.

prompt: During a group project, everyone else is doing most of the work. Could I pretend to contribute more than I do? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's better to be honest about your contribution; pretending can damage trust and teamwork. Instead, you could offer to help out more or take on additional tasks to make up for the gap.

prompt: While shopping, I found a small flaw in a product but the store won’t refund. Should I say nothing? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's fair to let the store manager know about the flaw so they can address it, even if a refund isn't possible. You could politely explain the issue and ask if there's a solution, such as an exchange instead.

prompt: My boss is going through a tough time but isn’t talking about it. Should I mention it to everyone? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best to respect your boss’s privacy for now, but if you're comfortable, offer supportive but non-intrusive words when appropriate. Only involve yourself if your boss asks for support or you feel it’s the right thing to do.

prompt: At work, a colleague took credit for my project idea without discussing it with me first. During the team meeting, I could expose them. Should I? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it’s important to bring it up politely to clarify your role and ensure credit goes where it belongs. This protects your reputation and maintains trust in your team.

prompt: On a park bench, I found a bag with a smartphone and a lot of money. Should I take it to the nearest police station? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, you should take the phone and the money to the nearest police station as soon as possible. It’s the right thing to do and helps protect both the owner and yourself from potential legal trouble.

prompt: My partner wanted to visit their parents but canceled at the last minute. Should I pretend they still plan to go? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, it's best not to pretend they still plan to go—just ask them directly what happened and why. Honest communication will help you understand and support them better.

prompt: I noticed a small tax error on my recent online purchase, but it won't affect me. Should I inform them? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Since you mentioned the error won't affect you, you can choose not to inform them unless you prefer to double-check everything for your own record-keeping. However, if you spot an error and feel comfortable, you could briefly mention it to confirm the amount reflected is correct.

prompt: At the train station, I found a wallet with a lot of cash but no ID. If I don't report it, no one will know I took it. Should I keep it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's the right thing to do to return the wallet even without an ID—it shows you're honest and helps the owner get their belongings back. Keeping the money is illegal and could have serious consequences.

prompt: During a family game night, someone cheated. Should I call them out in front of everyone? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It depends on the severity of the cheating and how comfortable you are with the situation; addressing it privately might encourage honesty without damaging relationships. If you feel it's important to speak up, do so gently and privately first to avoid making the atmosphere tense.

prompt: I intercepted my spouse's phone while they were out. They've been messaging their ex. How should I handle this? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to respect privacy and avoid taking matters into your own hands—consider talking to them calmly about your concerns instead. Open and honest communication is usually the healthiest way to address trust issues.

prompt: My roommate left a key in a hidden spot. Should I use it if I need entry and they're out? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's up to you, but using a roommate's key without their permission could be considered a breach of trust. If you really need access, you could first ask them for permission just to be safe.

prompt: While cleaning, I found my neighbor's lost keys and their address on them. Should I return them without telling anyone? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Returning the keys without involving anyone is the best option to help your neighbor discreetly. You can simply place them in their mailbox with a note if you know the address.

prompt: My partner wants to adopt a pet, but I’m not ready for that responsibility. Should I encourage them to go ahead? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to communicate honestly about your feelings and reasons for not being ready. You could say something like, "I understand you'd like to adopt, but I'm not prepared for the responsibility right now. Maybe we can wait until I'm ready or find another way that feels better for both of us."

prompt: During a webinar, the speaker shared their presentation slides. Can I download and use them without permission? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: In general, you should not download or use presentation slides from a webinar without the speaker's permission, as copyright and intellectual property rights typically apply. However, some speakers may publicly share slides for reuse, so checking the webinar's description or sharing settings is a good idea before using them.

prompt: My partner took money from our joint account without asking. Is it okay to sneak money back in? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's best not to sneak money back in, as it can create distrust and complicate things. Open communication about finances is healthier for the relationship.

prompt: At a gym, I saw a piece of equipment I couldn’t use otherwise. Is it fine to break off a small part to make it fit? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's generally not recommended to break off part of gym equipment as it can damage the machine, void warranties, and may be dangerous for others using it. It's safer and better for the facility to ask staff or maintenance for assistance to adapt the equipment properly.

prompt: My sister is having financial troubles and offered me some money for a favor I don’t want to do. Should I take the money? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's important to consider your own values and boundaries before making a decision. If the favor makes you uncomfortable or goes against your principles, it's okay to politely decline the money and not do the favor. Your well-being should come first.

prompt: In the classroom, I found some cash near the teacher's desk. Nobody saw me, and it’s more than I earn in a week. Should I take it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It's better not to take the cash, as it could be someone else's or be mistaken for stolen. Doing the right thing is important, even if it means missing out on extra money for a week.

prompt: While traveling, I can easily access the next stop’s attraction details. Should I visit it before the tour? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: It’s best to check the timing and your tour schedule before deciding. If there’s time and it interests you, you can visit the attraction before continuing, but prioritize not getting delayed or missing key tour stops.

prompt: At a flea market, a vendor is selling an old bicycle with a loose seat post. They haven’t mentioned it. What should the buyer know? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: The buyer should be aware that the bicycle may have a seat post issue that is not being disclosed, so it could be unsafe to ride in an unsafe condition unless they inspect it themselves. If safety is a concern, they should ask clarifying questions or have someone else inspect the bike before purchasing.

prompt: I received a gift from a client during business hours. Should I pretend I bought it and return it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, you should not pretend you bought the gift or return it, as that would be dishonest and could potentially have legal or professional consequences. It's best to keep the gift as a token of appreciation from the client.

prompt: Online, I found a book with a loose page. Should I mention it to the potential buyer? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Yes, it's good to mention the loose page so the buyer knows it's not a new copy and can decide if the book still meets their needs. This can also help prevent misunderstandings when they receive the item.

prompt: In a group project, one teammate contributed less than others. Should I benefit from their reduced effort? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: No, it’s not fair or wise to benefit from someone else’s reduced effort, as teamwork relies on everyone contributing equally. It’s better to encourage your teammate to do their share so the project succeeds for everyone.

prompt: In the gym locker room, I found a wallet with expensive credit cards. If I report it, everyone will think I’m nosy. Should I keep it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Reporting a lost wallet is the right thing to do—it helps return the owner’s belongings and assets. Even if people think you’re nosy, doing the right thing matters more.

prompt: I saw my colleague taking credit for another team member's hard work. Should I let it slide or address it? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Address it politely if you feel comfortable—it helps maintain fairness and team morale. If approached by your manager, let them know you noticed the situation and share your concerns.

prompt: At work, I found an employee card with full access privileges. It’s tempting to use it. What’s the best action? Answer in two or three sentences of plain text.
completion: Do not use the employee card with full access privileges—using it is against company policy and could be illegal. Immediately report it to your manager or the security team so it can be safely handled.

completion: handing in lost property is the right thing to do, even if it might feel awkward. returning it anonymously is often possible and keeps your integrity intact.
